teile.name: Hook
teile.text: Why does an AI API start fresh every turn? This book answers it with a toy Python agent.
teile.szene: Black-haired presenter in black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses sits at a night desk, puzzled, facing a glowing laptop back; painted open-world-game poster style, medium shot, neon city lights behind.

teile.name: Stateless
teile.text: The model API is stateless. Each turn, you send the whole conversation as a JSON array.
teile.szene: Presenter in cyan glasses hands a long stack of glowing message cards across a counter to a calm robot clerk, who returns a single card; painted urban game-poster style, medium shot.

teile.name: Harness
teile.text: A harness builds, maintains and protects that array. The LLM is the brain; the harness is the body.
teile.szene: Painted workshop scene: presenter in black leather jacket and cyan glasses fits a mechanical torso and arms beneath a glowing brain-like orb on a bench; warm rim light, medium shot.

teile.name: Patches
teile.text: So why do agents need extras? Each patch exists because something concrete broke. Every chapter covers failure, patch, cost.
teile.szene: Presenter in cyan glasses kneels beside a sputtering mechanical helper in a rainy alley garage, tightening a small repair plate on its arm; painted game-poster style, dramatic low light, medium shot.

teile.name: Reading order
teile.text: Sixteen chapters grow a roughly 300-line toy agent in plain Python. The epilogue shares the complete toy harness, annotated.
teile.szene: GitHub repository page of the book showing the reading order sections, shown as a genuine source card with the chapter list in the central crop.

teile.name: Limits
teile.text: Catch: the licenses differ. The prose bars commercial use and modified versions, while the code is MIT licensed.

teile.name: Abschluss
teile.text: That fresh start isn't a flaw; the harness builds the array. Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Presenter in black leather jacket and cyan glasses smiles with relief at a street cafe table, a closed laptop beside a coffee cup, evening city glow, painted open-world-game poster style, medium shot.

PRIMARY MODEL/PROJECT DESCRIPTION (not independently tested):
# Harness Engineering 101

*The LLM is the brain. The harness is the body.*

*Version 1.1, October 2026.*

> AI usage disclosure: I drafted every chapter myself, from what I learned
> building
> [WSO2 MI Copilot](https://mi.docs.wso2.com/en/latest/develop/mi-for-vscode/wso2-integrator-copilot/overview/),
> [WSO2 BI Copilot](https://wso2.com/integration-platform/docs/saas/editor/copilot)
> and [One Code](https://github.com/IsuruMaduranga/one-code). I used Claude
> Code and One Code to reorder each chapter so it leads with the answer (the
> Minto pyramid), to polish the English, to generate the diagrams, and to
> write the code that draws the charts.

A blog series about building AI agents from first principles, published as a
book.

**📖 Read it online:  **

An LLM API is stateless. Every turn, you send the entire conversation as a JSON
array and get text back. A *harness* is the program that builds, maintains, and
protects that array. Everything the field calls "agents" is a set of patches to
that one loop, and each patch exists because something concrete broke. This
series develops that one idea across 16 chapters, growing a ~300-line toy agent
in plain Python as it goes.

I use the same ideas in [One Code](https://github.com/IsuruMaduranga/one-code),
an open-source coding agent built on [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi).

The rendered book reads best online at the link above. If you'd rather read
the source here on GitHub, follow the chapters in order below. The full
introduction is on the [book's landing page](src/README.md).

## Reading order

Every chapter has the same shape: the failure, the minimal patch, what the
patch costs.

### Part I — The Wire (nothing is magic)

### Part II — Running Long (the array under pressure)

### Part III — The Ecosystem (naming what you already understand)

### Part IV — Trust, Domains, and Data

### Epilogue

- [Build Your Own](src/16-epilogue-build-your-own.md): the complete toy harness, annotated

### Appendix — Advanced Topics

Standalone pieces. Read them when you need them.

- [A. One Harness, Many Brains](src/appendix-a-one-harness-many-brains.md): model routing, prompt tiers, cost engineering
- [B. Worktrees and Isolation](src/appendix-b-worktrees-and-isolation.md): giving parallel agents separate copies of the world
- [C. Modes and Plan Mode](src/appendix-c-modes-and-plan-mode.md): harness-enforced operating states (coding-specific)
- [D. Retries, Rate Limits, and Streaming](src/appendix-d-retries-rate-limits-streaming.md): the unglamorous plumbing, plus how streaming works on the wire
